text: The question of whether artificial intelligence systems could be conscious or sentient is no longer confined to science fiction or armchair metaphysics. Contemporary AI systems can generate first-person reports, maintain extended dialogue, use tools, operate as agents, and interact through embodied or simulated interfaces. In robotics, these questions are especially salient because intelligent systems increasingly enter physical, social, clinical, educational, and collaborative environments. A robot that speaks, remembers, adapts, and acts in the world may elicit stronger attributions of mindedness than a disembodied language model, even when its mechanisms do not warrant such attributions.
source_label: Sentient AI in robots and agents: prolegomena for an evidence-based research program
